title: catalogueR
text: eQTL Catalogue includes large number standardised QTL datasets (110 datasets 20 studies 7/4/2020). actually contains just eQTL data. dataset, following kinds QTLs can queried: gene expression QTL: quant_method="ge" (default) quant_method="microarray", depending dataset. catalogueR automatically select whichever option available. exon expression QTL: construction quant_method="ge" transcript usage QTL: construction quant_method="tx" promoter, splice junction 3’ end usage QTL: construction quant_method="txrev"

title: catalogueR
text: can view metadata table current datasets: can search metadata datasets certain keywords (case-insensitive substrings across multiple columns).

title: catalogueR
text: Supply one paths GWAS summary stats files (one per locus) automatically download eQTL data within range. files can formats, either gzip-compressed (.gz) uncompressed: .csv, .tsv, space-separated. summary stats files must following column names (order matter): SNP (rsid SNP) CHR (chromosome; without “chr” prefix) POS (basepair position) … (optional extra columns) selected argument split_files=TRUE, query results distributed across multiple files saved disk. useful want load one massive data.table every time want look specific result subsets. scenario, eQTLcatalogue_query() returns list file paths (instead data.table ). merge files back together import R, use:
code: sumstats_paths <- echodata::get_Nalls2019_loci(limit_snps = 5) gwas.qtl_paths <- catalogueR::eQTLcatalogue_query(   sumstats_paths = sumstats_paths["BST1"],   qtl_search = c("Alasoo_2018.macrophage_naive"),   split_files = TRUE) GWAS.QTL <- catalogueR::merge_files(file_paths = gwas.qtl_paths)

title: catalogueR
text: can also make queries eQTL Catalogue manually specifying coordinates region want extract, well unique_label QTL dataset (see data("meta") IDs).
code: GWAS.QTL_manual <- catalogueR::eQTLcatalogue_fetch(   unique_label = "Alasoo_2018.macrophage_IFNg",   chrom = 8,   bp_lower = 21527069 - 500,   bp_upper = 21527069 + 500)

title: Colocalization
text: aim robustly test whether genetic signals underlying two datasets (e.g. GWAS vs. eQTL locus) indeed , using methodology called colocalization. Specifically, use coloc, infers probability SNP causal given locus datasets. tests hypothesis signals show substantially similar association distributions.

title: Colocalization
text: previously queried eQTL Catalogue using several Parkinson’s disease GWAS loci (eQTLcatalogue_query()). Let’s first gather files saved TSV files.
code: gwas.qtl_paths <- catalogueR::eQTLcatalogue_example_queries(fnames = c(   "BST1__Alasoo_2018.macrophage_IFNg+Salmonella.tsv.gz",   "BST1__Alasoo_2018.macrophage_naive.tsv.gz",   "BST1__Alasoo_2018.macrophage_Salmonella.tsv.gz" ))

title: Colocalization
text: Since original release, coloc updated can now model multiple causal variants within given dataset (see paper), whereas previously assume one causal variant. Thus, may able better estimate colocalization probability two datasets.
code: coloc_QTLs <- catalogueR::COLOC_run(   gwas.qtl_paths = gwas.qtl_paths,   top_snp_only = TRUE,   split_by_group = FALSE,   method = "abf")

title: Colocalization
text: First, let’s plot results >80% colocalization probability. colocalization threshold commonly used field. colocalizations >=80% probability, can lower threshold explore data (though advisable real analyses). many results: cases, may many colocalized results show plot . general rule, tests run higher probability threshold , since Bayesian methods calculate P-values (thus use multiple-testing correction methods like FDR). example, ran many thousands coloc tests across many GWAS-eQTL pairs, advisable raise PP threshold 0.90 even 0.99. also benefit narrowing (sometimes many!) results may focus strongest colocalizations.
code: coloc_plot <- catalogueR::COLOC_heatmap(   coloc_QTLs = coloc_QTLs,   coloc_thresh = .8) coloc_plot <- catalogueR::COLOC_heatmap(   coloc_QTLs = coloc_QTLs,   coloc_thresh = 0)

text: library(dplyr) paths <- catalogueR::eQTLcatalogue_example_queries() query <- paths["BST1__Alasoo_2018.macrophage_IFNg"] qtl.egene <- data.frame(     query     )[, grep("*.QTL$|dataset_id|SNP",              colnames(query), value = TRUE)] sorted_egenes <- qtl.egene |>     dplyr::group_by(gene.QTL) |>     dplyr::summarise(mean.P = mean(pvalue.QTL), min.P = min(pvalue.QTL)) |>     dplyr::arrange(min.P) qtl.egene <- subset(qtl.egene, gene.QTL == sorted_egenes$gene.QTL[1]) gwas.region <- data.frame(     query     )[, grep("*.QTL$|dataset_id",              colnames(query),              value = TRUE, invert = TRUE)] #### Run #### coloc_res <- catalogueR:::COLOC_get_res(qtl.egene = qtl.egene,                                      gwas.region = gwas.region)

text: gwas.qtl_paths Query results paths eQTLcatalogue_query. save_path save results . top_snp_only include SNP (highest SNP-wise PP.H4, usually one smallest p-value) instead SNPs. Can useful reducing data size. split_by_group Split files QTL group saving. method Method querying eQTL Catalogue: REST (default) Uses REST API. Slow can used anyone. tabix Uses tabix query. Fast, requires user first get IP address whitelisted EMBL-EBI server admin putting request . Note: "tabix" ~17x faster REST API,  currently far less reliable method REST API  tabix tends get blocked eQTL Catalogue's firewall. See details. coloc_thresh Colocalization Posterior Probability threshold,  using formula: (PP.H3 + PP.H4 >= coloc_thresh) & (PP.H4 / PP.H3 >= 2). compute_n compute per-SNP sample size (new column "N"). column "N" already present dat, column used extract per-SNP sample sizes argument compute_n ignored. column "N" present dat, one following options can supplied compute_n: 0 N computed. >0 number >0 provided, value set N every row. **Note**: Computing N way incorrect avoided possible. "sum" N computed : cases (N_CAS) + controls (N_CON), long columns present. "ldsc" N computed effective sample size: Neff =(N_CAS+N_CON)*(N_CAS/(N_CAS+N_CON)) / mean((N_CAS/(N_CAS+N_CON))(N_CAS+N_CON)==max(N_CAS+N_CON)). "giant" N computed effective sample size: Neff = 2 / (1/N_CAS + 1/N_CON). "metal" N computed effective sample size: Neff = 4 / (1/N_CAS + 1/N_CON). nThread number CPU cores want use speed queries parallelization. verbose Print messages.
